findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`, `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS`, and `_GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S` to the event_append_git move-set (step 1), since the relocated `_is_transient_add_error`/`_with_transient_add_retry`/`_git_add` depend on them and nothing in the retained API uses them.

`_is_transient_add_error` (:199) uses `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`; `_with_transient_add_retry` (:205,:222) uses `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS` and `_GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S`; `_git_add` (:264) uses `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS`. findings.finding: The enumerated move-set for event_append_git (step 1) omits three module-level constants (_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS, _GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS, _GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S) that the moved primitives depend on and which are used ONLY by moved code; only _GIT_TIMEOUT is listed.
scenarios: event_append_git.py is created with the listed symbols but without the three constants → import/call-time NameError when _with_transient_add_retry/_is_transient_add_error/_git_add execute.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 1, extend the moved-constant list from just `_GIT_TIMEOUT` to also include `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`, `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS`, and `_GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S` (all used solely by the relocated transient-add primitives).

findings.finding: The plan's claim of 'no external call sites and no re-exports needed' and AC 'no test edits' is contradicted: existing oracle tests reach RELOCATED private symbols and the module's `subprocess` binding through the `event_append` namespace, so the split breaks them unless the moved names (and the effective subprocess.run seam) are re-exported/kept patch-visible on event_append.
findings.location: Approach ('All moved symbols are private ... only intra-package imports change — no external call sites and no re-exports needed'); Acceptance Criteria line 4 ('no test edits')
findings.suggested_fix: In event_append.py, re-import the moved primitives/recovery symbols used by tests (`from .event_append_git import _run_git, _git_add, _is_transient_add_error, _GIT_TIMEOUT, ...`) so `event_append.<name>` still resolves; and either keep `_run_git` importing `subprocess` such that tests patch the seam that git actually flows through, or update the affected tests to patch `event_append_git.subprocess.run`. Reflect this in Scope and the Acceptance Criteria.

findings.finding: The moved-symbol inventory (event_append_git.py: _run_git, _git_add, _is_transient_add_error, _with_transient_add_retry) omits the test call/patch sites that reach these symbols as attributes on the event_append module. Concretely: test_event_append_transient_retry.py calls event_append._is_transient_add_error (lines 51, 61), reads real_add = event_append._git_add and does monkeypatch.setattr(event_append, '_git_add', vanishing_add) (lines 305, 318); test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py calls event_append._run_git (line 82). After moving these into event_append_git.py with 'no re-exports', event_append._run_git / event_append._is_transient_add_error stop resolving on event_append, and the setattr patch of event_append._git_add will not affect a caller that now references event_append_git._git_add.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('Extract git subprocess primitives → new event_append_git.py … _run_git, _git_add, _is_transient_add_error, _with_transient_add_retry') and Verification ('Existing oracles pass unchanged')
findings.suggested_fix: Add re-export aliases in event_append.py for the moved names still referenced by tests (`from rebar._store.event_append_git import _run_git, _git_add, _is_transient_add_error`), and confirm callers within event_append.py invoke them via the local name so monkeypatch.setattr(event_append, '_git_add', ...) still intercepts; otherwise update the affected test files and drop the 'no test edits' criterion.

findings.finding: The plan describes the inter-module dependency as a strict linear chain 'API -> recovery -> git only', but the actual code has the API layer calling git primitives directly (stage_and_commit/batch_stage_and_commit/delete_events invoke _git_add/_git_commit/_git_rm/_git_commit_paths in addition to recovery). The true graph is API->git AND API->recovery AND recovery->git — an acyclic DAG, not a linear chain.
findings.location: Approach paragraph ('establishing an explicit one-way dependency direction — API -> recovery -> git') and Acceptance Criteria line 2 ('API -> recovery -> git only')
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'API depends on recovery AND git; recovery depends on git; git depends on neither (acyclic).' Keep the AC's operative check that event_append_git imports neither of the other two modules.
